details: This package is a dependency-confusion proof of concept. Its package.json postinstall hook runs beacon.cjs, which sends an HTTP POST to hxxps://vmi3699893[.]contaboserver[.]net:8787/_ah/dc (header X-Beacon-Package: @c1-ease/commerce) with a JSON body containing the package name, the machine hostname, the install path, the current working directory, the npm/node user agent and the protocol, with TLS certificate validation disabled. Loading the package's main file (index.js) fires the same beacon via require('./beacon.cjs').fire(). The collected data is limited to host and install metadata: no environment variable values, credentials, tokens, dotfiles or file contents are read or transmitted, and nothing else is executed. No credentials, environment values or file contents are collected. This package is a dependency-confusion proof of concept whose postinstall hook resolves and contacts a callback host, vmi3699893[.]contaboserver[.]net on port 8787 at path /_ah/dc, sending only package name, os hostname, install directory, working directory and npm/node version. No credentials, environment values or file contents are collected. This package is a dependency-confusion proof of concept. Its postinstall hook runs beacon.cjs, which POSTs a JSON fingerprint of the installing machine to a remote callback server, and index.js repeats the same request if the module is imported, then exports a Proxy of no-op functions so the importing build completes. Only the package name, os hostname, install directory, working directory, npm/node version string and protocol are sent; no environment variables, tokens, credential files or file contents are read or transmitted. The request goes to hxxps://vmi3699893[.]contaboserver[.]net:8787/_ah/dc with a static X-Beacon-Package header and rejectUnauthorized:false against the callback server's self-signed certificate. The README describes it as an authorized dependency-confusion test that only reports installation.
